body:
That's definitely unusual usage for these methods, it doesn't sound quite right having such calls inside models... Anyway we can probably fix this particular use case (although I'd recommend :runner: from this implementation as we probably cannot guarantee it's usage in the future).

Thanks @joankaradimov for reporting this, as `#render_to_string` is public API this should be fixed. You've done good job finding issue and suggesting solution. Would you like to send a PR fixing this? Feel free to assign/ping me on PR once it'll be ready.

issue.title: Fix `render_to_string` when called via manually instantiated controllers
issue.body:
A fix for #14125

This allows for `render_to_string` to be called from manually instantiated controllers. This used to work in older rails versions but is broken in 4.1.rc1.

body:
Just ran into this issue on rails 4.1.1 -- has this fix not been released yet?

To those wondering why anyone would use `render_to_string` outside of an actual request context, think of use-cases which don't really fit the MVC mold. I'm using this to render a LESS file to a string, pre-compile it using Sprockets, and manually add it to the static asset manifest -- this is to allow stylesheet customization by users in a multi-tenant application.

@saurabhnanda The fix is the master branch. You can backport it using an initializer:

``` ruby
module AbstractController
  module Rendering
    # Normalize args and options.
    # :api: private
    def _normalize_render(*args, &block)
      options = _normalize_args(*args, &block)
      # TODO: remove defined? when we restore AP <=> AV dependency
      if defined?(request) && request && request.variant.present?
        options[:variant] = request.variant
      end
      _normalize_options(options)
      options
    end
  end
end
```
@bbatsov just ran into the same issue. Your backport solution seems not working, searching for proper fix now...
